candidates.name: Existing AutoLoop durable execution (STACK_A)
candidates.persistenceModel: append-only evidence journal with explicit hash chain (src/evidence/run-evidence-store.mjs) + atomic CURRENT.json checkpoint (src/c2d/checkpoint-store.mjs: checksum + CAS revision + structured lock + write permit) + fingerprint chain (repo/input/config/IR/DAG) + final manifest with artifact inventory
candidates.replaySemantics: resume from safe checkpoint; completed phases never re-run; read-only interrupted phase requeued; writer -> fail closed; pre-decomposition -> RESTART_REQUIRED
candidates.retryModel: bounded repair loop in lifecycle-runner (maxRepairAttempts 0|1), attempt persisted
candidates.idempotencyModel: journal-first; terminal runs return COMPLETE on repeated resume; result artifacts sha256-pinned
candidates.failureRecovery: resumeAutoLoop API; repository/input/config/IR/DAG fingerprints all fail closed
candidates.timers: timeoutMs per phase; frozen in config fingerprint
candidates.longRunning: phase-scoped; no durable timers/sleeps across restart
candidates.versioning: checkpoint format major check; sourceHashes in config fingerprint reject source drift

candidates.name: Temporal
candidates.persistenceModel: Temporal Server (frontend/history/matching/worker) with DB backend: SQLite (dev), PostgreSQL, MySQL; workflow history event store; task queues
candidates.replaySemantics: deterministic workflow replay: workflow code must be deterministic (pure, no IO); all IO must be in Activities; replay reconstructs state from history
candidates.idempotencyModel: activity idempotency via workflow logic; exactly-once for workflow commands; at-least-once for activities (side-effect idempotency is the app's job)
candidates.failureRecovery: server-managed; worker crash -> tasks re-dispatched; workflow continues from last event
candidates.localDeployment: docker compose (server + DB); dev server with SQLite
candidates.operationalComplexity: medium-high: new service(s) + DB; versioning/upgrades; namespace management
candidates.sandboxIntegration: activities can spawn containers; workflow sandboxing rules for determinism
candidates.longRunning: first-class long-running workflows; signals; child workflows
candidates.versioning: workflow versioning (patch API, worker version sets) — a real operational burden
candidates.rollback: must remove service + DB; workflow code version pinning
candidates.fitNotes: Would replace AutoLoop's own journal/checkpoint with a server+DB. AutoLoop's model adapters are inherently non-deterministic IO -> must all be Activities (already the case in effect). Adds a service dependency + DB for a correctness need that STACK_A already covers in-process; the marginal benefit is durable timers/long-running workflows and server-side retry, none of which AutoLoop's current graph model requires.

candidates.name: Restate
candidates.persistenceModel: Restate server with journaled invocations; storage: embedded RocksDB (single node) or PostgreSQL; virtual objects + services; each invocation journaled
candidates.replaySemantics: durable execution via journaled invocation; service handlers are re-executed on retry with journal replay; journaling of deterministic steps
candidates.idempotencyModel: exactly-once semantics claimed for request-response/one-way/scheduled; journal + dedup
candidates.failureRecovery: server-managed; client/worker crash -> invocation replayed from journal
candidates.localDeployment: single binary / docker; rocksdb single-node default
candidates.operationalComplexity: medium: one server process; versioning of services
candidates.sandboxIntegration: handlers run in your process; container spawning is app-level
candidates.longRunning: virtual objects + durable promises; long-running invocations
candidates.licensing: SDK MIT; SERVER is BSL (Business Source License — source-available, NOT OSI open source)
supplyChainFindings: @restatedev/restate-server depends on @scarf/scarf (^1.4.0) — a third-party analytics/telemetry package that phones home by default (verified from npm registry dependencies metadata). This conflicts with AutoLoop's privacy/security posture (COST-1/CBM security contract: no unexplained network behavior; telemetry must be explicit and validated).
candidates.rollback: remove server + storage; journal semantics bound to server version
candidates.fitNotes: Journal-based durable execution closest in spirit to STACK_A, but requires a server process + RocksDB/Postgres; the BSL server license and bundled Scarf telemetry are blockers under Stage 13 rules (candidate must not be adopted when unexplained network behavior exists) unless independently mitigated.
